A PERT prior from a posterior distribution

Source: R/efsa.R
fitpert.Rd

Fits a PERT distribution to the posterior distribution of a parameter, e.g. the model-averaged BMD of bmdbayes, as an informative prior for the analysis of a new study (Kremer et al. 2026, EFSA EN-9902): the posterior is summarised by 1000 quantiles; the minimum and maximum of the PERT are their smallest and largest value (the 0.05% and 99.95% quantiles), so that the prior excludes values outside them; the mode is the mode of their kernel density, and the shape is estimated by maximum likelihood (between 0 and 20). Several posteriors, e.g. of several historical studies, are mixed with equal weights, the recommended way to combine studies. With discounting, the shape is reduced so that the variance of the PERT doubles (approximately, as the shape is at least 1e-4).

Usage

fitpert(..., weights = NULL, discount = FALSE)

Arguments

...

bmdbayes objects (the posterior of the BMD), or numeric vectors of posterior draws

weights

for a single numeric vector of draws, their weights (e.g. of importance sampling)

discount

logical, discount the prior (double its variance)

Value

a prior (see priors), e.g. for prior=list(bmd=...) of drmTMB or the bmd argument of efsapriors

References

Kremer, C., Saenen, N. D., Bijnens, K., Faes, C., De Boever, P., Smeets, K. and Aerts, M. (2026). Compilation of NTP and published dose-response data: study of informative priors in the EFSA platform for Bayesian benchmark dose analysis. EFSA Supporting Publications, EN-9902.

See also

bmdefsa, bmdbayes, efsapriors, priors

Examples

# a PERT prior from posterior draws of a BMD
set.seed(1)
draws <- exp(rnorm(2000, log(2), 0.3))
fitpert(draws)
#> pert(0.762757, 1.83879, 5.95985, shape=6.20185) 

# from the model-averaged posterior of the BMD of bmdbayes (or bmdefsa), e.g. of a historical
# study, as an informative prior of the BMD for a current study
pr <- list(bmd = pert(0.1, 1, 5), b2 = normal(8, 1), b3 = normal(-2, 2), sigma = half_normal(1))
fit <- function(model)
  drmTMB(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = model,
         start = c(b1 = 0, b5 = 0), fix = c(b1 = TRUE, b5 = TRUE),
         bmdpar = list(bmr = 0.05, def = "relative"), prior = pr)
ba <- bmdbayes(LL = fit("loglogistic"), W2 = fit("weibull2"))
fitpert(ba)
#> pert(0.636195, 1.34061, 1.87419, shape=4.20974)
